text:
I had my wisdom tooth extracted at this clinic, but four days after the surgery, I experienced extremely severe pain that radiated to my eye, almost unbearable. I called the clinic and came in for an examination, but all I received was a wound cleaning.
On the fifth day, the pain was still severe and hadn't improved. I called again to request an appointment with the doctor for medication, but the clinic refused, citing a full schedule, even though they had a doctor available who couldn't help a patient in such severe pain. I had to go to another clinic for medication at my own expense.
The worst part is:
On the seventh day, when I went to have the stitches removed, I found out that the doctor in charge of my case had "prescribed pain medication since the fourth day when the pain began," but the clinic neglected to provide it. Because the clinic didn't have the prescribed medication, the doctor had to switch to a different type of medication, requiring me to travel to the clinic "almost daily" to change and receive the new medication. This resulted in wasted time, travel expenses, and significantly impacted my life.
This means I suffered severe pain for many days when there was a solution available from the beginning, but the clinic failed to implement it. This is a case of negligence, patient neglect, and poor internal management. It has caused me to lose confidence in this clinic. The doctor in charge of my case and the assistants were very good. However, there could be some coordination issues within the clinic.
The clinic wasn't able to adequately care for patients in emergency pain situations. This needs urgent improvement.
